classification.difficultyReason: Substitute each shoe size into the supplied equation and round to the nearest centimetre, then classify the prediction by comparing the shoe size with the explicitly stated range 6–13. Both decisions directly apply taught methods.

content.prompt:
Data was collected on 100 adults comparing shoe size and height. Shoe sizes ranged from 6 to 13. An equation relating height (in cm) to shoe size was determined to be:

$$\text{height}=127.18+4.84\times\text{shoe size}$$

Use this equation to predict (to the nearest cm) the height of a person whose shoe size is as follows. Are you interpolating or extrapolating?

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the predicted height in cm.

$$\begin{align*}h&=127.18+4.84\times7\\h&=161.06\\h&\approx161\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Interpolation, since $7$ lies within the observed shoe-size range $6$ to $13$.

Let $h$ be the predicted height in cm.

$$\begin{align*}h&=127.18+4.84\times12\\h&=185.26\\h&\approx185\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Interpolation, since $12$ lies within the observed shoe-size range $6$ to $13$.

Let $h$ be the predicted height in cm.

$$\begin{align*}h&=127.18+4.84\times14\\h&=194.94\\h&\approx195\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Extrapolation, since $14$ exceeds the largest observed shoe size, $13$.
